prompt: Melodic dungeon exploration music for a 1990s first-person dark fantasy game, for haunted halls and forgotten libraries. A slow, eerie waltz in 3/4 time, around 100 BPM, in C sharp minor, uncanny and wary rather than sad. A celesta and a glockenspiel tick out an interlocking music-box ostinato that never stops, pizzicato strings pluck the chords on every beat, a plucked contrabass marks each downbeat, and a soft woodblock ticks like a clock. Over them a melody is always being played, passed between a solo violin and a bassoon in long phrases, with a muted trumpet answering now and then. No horns, no clarinet, no harp, no dulcimer, no marimba. Something is always moving: no drones, no long held notes on their own, no ambient washes or pads. Sounds like a General MIDI orchestral soundtrack played through a 1990s sound card wavetable: slightly synthetic, clean, no modern cinematic bombast. Keeps the same instruments and energy all the way through, one even texture: no intro, no big build, no ending or fade-out, as it will loop for as long as the player explores.
